summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console features focused on tracing narrative, error analysis, and runbook orchestration for SparrowTech's customer support assistant. Covered how traces stitch request logs, KV cache fallback visibility, request replays, and fallthrough policies interact with Dedicated vs Hosted options. Agreed next steps for pilot data handoff and security paperwork.
topics: Data residency and KMS/SAML security questions
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08 15:30 PST
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Recorded by Fireflies.ai

00:00 Jordan (AE): All right hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood Inference, I'll hand off to Priya in a sec to do the walkthrough. We have Marcus with me too. Can folks introduce real quick?
00:12 Maya (SparrowTech - Head of Platform): Maya here, head of platform at SparrowTech. We're primarily looking at how we surface failure modes from our customer assistant pipeline.
00:18 Alex Chen (Platform Eng): Alex, I run the infra for the assistant stack. We'll be most interested in traces and request-level debugging.
00:24 Darren (SRE): Darren, SRE - we'll care a lot about tail latency and fallbacks.
00:27 Nina (Security): Nina, security. I'll be asking about KMS, audit logs, and SOC two stuff.
00:32 Jordan: Great thanks. Priya, take it away?
00:35 Priya (SE): Sure thanks. Uh quick agenda: we'll start with the trace-narrative in the Console, then show how request logs, KV cache and replay tie together, and finish with runbook automation —canary fallback policies, and a quick note on hosted vs dedicate costs. If you want us to pause and jump to a specific sample trace say so.
00:50 Alex: We'll want to see an example where the KV cache missed and caused a long tail.
00:53 Priya: Perfect, I have one preloaded.
01:00 [Screen share begins - Redwood Console visible]
01:10 Priya: Ok here's the Request Map. This top lane is the overall narrative, it stitches events from the API gateway, the model runtime, and your downstream logging. Sometimes the transcription calls this the "narrative trace" or "trace timeline". Note that in some exports it was mis-labeled as 'Redwood Trace Narrate' in older builds.
01:28 Maya: Why are there gaps at 11:42 and 11:44? Looks like missing spans.
01:33 Priya: Those are where the KV cache returned empty and we fell back to a cold model call; the console marks them as Cache-Miss spans. The trace view has a little diff that shows token-by-token latency and where KV cached prefix was applied.
01:48 Darren: Can we correlate that with the API logs?
01:52 Priya: Yep - if you open the request detail there's a "Logs" tab. I'll click it. Here you can see the API gateway logs, the runtime logs, and the raw request payload. We stitch by request id, though sometimes if your front proxy rewrites headers the trace id can be munged — we've seen customers call it "X-Req-Id" vs "request-id" issues.
02:12 Alex: That happened to us once, so that explains gaps.
02:15 Priya: Also note the console attempts to auto-repair traces — when it sees similar timestamps it will attempt to join them heuristically, that process is called "trace stitching" in the UI.
02:28 Jordan: Quick question from me — can the stitching be disabled for sensitive logs? We need to avoid PII cross-correlation in some regs.
02:34 Priya: Yes, you can disable stitching at the org level, and mask fields in the Logs tab. We support field redaction and column filters; the policy can be pushed from the Private control plane if you're on Redwood Private.
02:47 Nina: On KMS — where are keys managed for Private? We need HSM-backed keys.
02:52 Priya: Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption with our service-managed keys but can integrate with customer KMS for enterprise tiers. I'll attach the security whitepaper.
03:06 Nina: And SAML/SSO is supported?
03:09 Marcus (SE): Yes SAML SSO plus SCIM for group sync. We also emit audit events for all console actions that can be forwarded to your SIEM.
03:20 Alex: Back to the trace — that KV miss, how do we see why it missed? Was it TTL, mismatch, serialization?
03:26 Priya: The detail view includes the cache metadata. In this example it shows a 304 TTL expiry and a serialization mismatch note — our runtime logs the exact key hash the model expects (though sometimes it's truncated in export so the UI shows a human-friendly hint).
03:41 Darren: Is that hash something we can use to retro-run a parity test?
03:44 Priya: Yes, you can export the raw key and rehydrate a local cache for replay tests. There's a "Prepare Parity Replay" action that packages the request and the cache key metadata.
03:57 Samir (PM): How does request replay interact with the billing/quotas? If we replay a lot, do we get charged as new tokens?
04:05 Priya: Replays are routed through a special replay lane; they can be billed as metered or marked as free for internal debug work depending on your contract. For pilots we can enable no-charge replays up to X tokens. We'll clarify in the pilot SOW.
04:20 Maya: Show us an example of runbook automation — we want automatic reroutes to a smaller model on cache miss to maintain latency SLOs.
04:27 Priya: Sure — here's the Rollouts/Policies tab. You can define a policy: if tail latency > 350ms and cache-miss rate > 20% then route to the smaller-quantized model for 5 minutes and notify on-call.
04:43 Alex: Is that per-route? We have multiple endpoints with different SLAs.
04:46 Priya: Yes per-route. You can attach policies to API keys or to model routes. Policies also support canary percentages and automatic rollback if quality regressions are detected by your eval set.
04:58 Darren: How do we track quality regressions? We need automated tests.
05:02 Priya: The Optimize product hooks into Eval sets; you can upload prompt/eval pairs and the system will run A/B comparisons and generate a regression score. It surfaces diffs in the runbook so you can abort a fallback if the quality delta is too large.
05:18 Jordan: Quick interjection — pricing tradeoffs here: dedicated capacity will give you more predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale, but Hosted is faster to start.
05:29 Maya: Cost is important but our first must is uptime and data separation. Dedicated looks likely.
05:35 Nina: For Dedicated what audit evidence do you provide?
05:38 Marcus: We provide SOC2 type II report, exportable audit logs, and a deployment manifest you can use for attestation. For Private on-prem we also support offline attestation.
05:50 Alex: Show us a real-world failure path — maybe a model OOM causing fallback to a smaller model and then cascade to a stale cache.
05:58 Priya: Ok here's a sample trace where the runtime threw an OOM at step 3. The console shows the error with a stack snippet (sometimes truncated as our runtime strips internal pointers), the automatic fallback triggered and we routed to a half-precision quantized variant. The trace notes show a subsequent spike in token latency because the fallback didn't have the warmed KV cache.
06:20 Darren: Can the runbook warm caches proactively after a fallback?
06:24 Priya: Yes — there's a background warm policy in the runbooks. After a fallback to smaller model we can schedule a warmed prefetch of frequent prompts, and the console will surface the warming progress. You can see metrics per warm job.
06:38 Alex: How long does warming take? Depends on sequence length, right?
06:42 Priya: Correct. We show estimated warm time and a confidence band. For typical 128-token prompts it can be seconds; for longer contexts it may be tens of seconds.
06:52 Samir: Any limitations on replaying traces that include PII?
06:55 Priya: You can enable PII scrubbers; the console redact options detect emails, phone numbers, and configurable patterns. For regulated work we recommend doing replays in Private with redaction at ingress.
07:10 [Timestamps jump as demo clicks through multiple traces quickly]
07:30 Alex: The timeline view is neat. One odd thing: some of our logs are in GCP stackdriver with slightly different timestamp formats — how robust is the ingestion?
07:40 Priya: We support a range of log formats, and we do a best-effort timestamp normalization. Ingest adapters can be customized; for very custom formats we can provide a small mapping runner.
07:52 Nina: On the SIEM side, can audit logs be forwarded to Splunk/Elastic?
07:56 Marcus: Yes, audit events and alerts can be pushed to Splunk/Elastic via webhook or native connector.
08:05 Maya: If we wanted an on-prem agent to collect traces and send them to your private control plane, is that supported?
08:12 Priya: We have a lightweight collector for Private — it can run in a fenced network and forward only metadata, or full payloads if you want. For air-gapped deployments we can package a tarball for offline ingestion.
08:26 Alex: Let's talk about integratability with our incident tool — we use PagerDuty + OpsGenie; can the console open incidents automatically?
08:33 Priya: Yes we have native PagerDuty integration and a generic webhook. You can trigger runbook steps automatically or require manual approval.
08:44 Samir: What's the latency to create an incident after trace detection?
08:47 Priya: Typically sub-10s from detection to webhook; depends on your on-call policies.
08:53 Jordan: We've covered a lot of platform questions — maybe walk through one full example end-to-end: detection, automation, replay, and postmortem.
08:58 Priya: Sure, I'll pick a single incident. Step one: detection, an anomaly detector flags a 95th percentile spike on route /assistant/respond. That generates an alert and a trace is created. The trace Narrative links the failure span to the model runtime error and marks a cache-miss. Runbook policy executes: route to quantized-2 at 50% and send PagerDuty. We then kick off a parity replay job to validate the fallback quality. After the replay, the Optimize eval shows a 3% quality drop, so runbook auto-rollback runs. The postmortem is auto-generated draft with spans, timelines, and recommended remediation (increase cache TTL, prefetch popular prompts).
09:43 Maya: Nice. In our world we'd probably want the postmortem exported to Confluence.
09:47 Priya: There's an export connector and also a markdown export you can push to any downstream.
09:54 Alex: On replay job scale — if we want to run thousands of replays for regression tests, can we parallelize?
09:59 Priya: Replays can be parallelized across Dedicated pools; we also have an offline batch runner for large regression workloads.
10:10 Darren: A note on observability: can the console link to raw GPU metrics for the node that served the request?
10:15 Marcus: Yes, for Dedicated we surface node-level telemetry (GPU utilization, memory, swap) and link to the infra provider. For Hosted we surface a subset of telemetry.
10:26 Nina: For compliance we'll need retention window options and the ability to purge customer data.
10:30 Priya: Retention and purge are configurable per-tenant; Private gives you full control. Hosted tiers have configurable retention up to X days, and we support on-request purge via API.
10:43 Samir: Ok let's talk logistics for the pilot — we'll provide 48 hours of request logs and a deck of critical prompts. What's the rough timeline?
10:51 Jordan: If we get the logs by the 12th, we can run a staging benchmark and have a pilot kickoff by the 20th.
10:57 Maya: Who will own security review?
10:60 Nina: (laugh) I think you mean 11:00 — I'm the security owner, I'll need the SOC2 and KMS design.
11:02 Jordan: We'll attach the security pack. Priya will also send the runbook slides and a sample trace export.
11:10 [Short silence while attendees skim the shared deck]
11:18 Alex: One more question — do you support model variants with different quantization formats? We use int8 and sometimes mixed precision.
11:24 Priya: Yes, we support a catalog of quantization profiles and the runtime will pick the optimal kernels. Note: older runtimes might label quant profiles as Q8-small in the UI which confused a customer, that's been fixed in the next patch.
11:38 Darren: Any gotchas when mixing models across regions? We have EU data residency requirements.
11:43 Priya: You can pin routes to region-specific pools. For EU-only data we recommend Private or a Dedicated EU cluster. The Console will surface region mismatch warnings if a route receives cross-region traffic.
11:57 Maya: Great. We're almost out of time — let's recap next steps.
12:01 Jordan: Recap: Priya sends runbook deck + trace export; SparrowTech shares 48-hour logs; Nina confirms compliance docs; Jordan schedules pilot kickoff.
12:12 Priya: I'll also include a short video showing the replay flow for your engineers.
12:18 Maya: Perfect thanks everyone.
12:22 Jordan: Thanks, we'll follow up with the calendar invite for the kickoff.
12:26 [Meeting ends]
